Dawn on a ferry ghat in Varanasi, mist on the Ganga. Mohan (70s), a lifelong boatman, is oiling his wooden boat when his son Tarun (40s), back from years of work abroad, arrives in a pressed shirt with a buyer's offer for the boat in his pocket. They speak around it, about the mist, about the rower Tarun never became. Tarun finally says he has come to sell. Mohan says nothing, stands, and puts the old oar into his son's hands. Tarun pushes the boat off the step and rows out a few strokes into the mist while Mohan watches from the ghat, then calls out, quietly, to bring it back before the sun is up.
